thesis_summary.thesis: DaVita Inc. (NYSE: DVA) operates kidney dialysis centers and related lab services for patients with chronic kidney failure, primarily in the United States. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$13.64 billion** and operating income was **$2.04 billion**. **[Fact]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$1.89 billion** and capital spending was **$0.58 billion**, leaving **$1.31 billion** of normalized owner earnings. **[Fact]** The company reports a **single operating segment** (U.S. dialysis and related lab services). **[Inference]** DaVita is a scale-driven healthcare operator whose economics depend on treatment volumes, payer mix (Medicare, Medicare Advantage, commercial), and disciplined center-level cost control.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The market may be pricing **durable dialysis demand and operating leverage** while underweighting **$10.5 billion of long-term debt and capital lease obligations** on the March 2026 balance sheet and **thin GAAP equity** (**$651 million** of stockholders equity at year-end 2025). **[Inference]** At **$179.17**, the stock trades below our base proof value per share (**$218**) after refreshing debt from filings, implying modest positive return at price if reinvestment assumptions hold. Berkshire Hathaway has held a large activist stake (SC-13D/A filings, context tier only); that signal supports quality-of-business but does not, by itself, justify ignoring net debt.
